package.author: Patrick R
package.description: Local speech-to-text dictation for Windows. Press a key, speak, and the words land in the field you were typing in.

en-US.author: Patrick R
en-US.description: Local speech-to-text dictation for Windows. Press a key, speak, and the words land in the field you were typing in.
en-US.longDescription:
Handy Tool is a local-first dictation tool for Windows. Press a key, speak, and the text is
delivered into whatever field you were working in.

Transcription runs on your machine using local Whisper, Parakeet, Moonshine or SenseVoice
models, with GPU acceleration through Vulkan. No account is required and no audio or
transcript leaves the machine unless you configure a remote provider.

It also includes push-to-talk, a transcribe-and-submit mode, a keyboard typer for contexts
where pasting is blocked, and a window-anchoring system for delivering dictation into a
specific window across multiple screens or remote desktop sessions.

Handy Tool is a fork of Handy by CJ Pais, developed independently.
en-US.name: Handy Tool
en-US.releaseNotes:
Fixed
- Speakers on this PC failed with "Could not find an implementation for ConvInteger(10)".
  The 141 MB int8 export of the speakers model uses integer convolutions that the ONNX Runtime
  bundled with Handy cannot run, so every speakers job on this PC failed. Handy now downloads the
  full-precision export (492 MB, same pinned revision, checked by SHA-256), which runs everywhere
  and is about three times faster on a CPU. The unusable 141 MB file is deleted automatically;
  download the model again in Advanced settings › Speakers (or on the Models page).
- "Paste the text with speakers" failed silently. When the speakers could not be found before
  the paste, the plain text was pasted with only a log line; it now also shows a warning.
